Date: 2026-05-14
Time: 15:00 PDT / Zoom
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Rios (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Jill Moreno (Peregrine Procurement), Rajiv Singh (Peregrine Security), Ellen Park (Peregrine Legal)
Recording: https://redwood.zoom/rec/ff-20260514-7329
summary: Procurement call to review MSA/DPA redlines, discuss SLA targets and credits, clarify security artifacts (SOC2/ISO, KMS, audit logs), and agree next steps for pricing approval and a technical benchmark. Redwood AE/SE to provide redlined agreements, security package, and run a workload benchmark; Peregrine legal/procurement to provide required DPA edits and sign-off timeline.
topics: MSA redlines and key legal asks
SLA targets, p95/p99 latency and credits
Pricing structure and committed usage discounts
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Rios: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you taking the time. on our side I'm Maya, AE, and Samir's our solutions engineer. quick confirm on roles?
[00:06] Jill Moreno: Yep Jill here, procurement.
[00:08] Rajiv Singh: Rajiv, security.
[00:10] Ellen Park: Ellen, legal.
[00:12] Samir Patel: quick agenda, redlines on MSA/DPA, SLAs, pricing approvals, and technical bench. sound good?
[00:18] Jill Moreno: sounds good. we need to move fast — budget committee wants vendor decisions by end of month if possible.
[00:25] Maya Rios: understood, that's doable as long as we get a couple items clarified — main ones being DPA encryption language and SLA credits.
[00:33] Ellen Park: on the DPA we have three non-negotiables: encrypted at rest with customer KMS, ability to audit log access for 2 years, and a standard data deletion clause. the redline we sent had some language we need addressed.
[00:45] Maya Rios: yes, we saw that redline. to clarify, Redwood supports customer-managed KMS and HSM integrations; we can do envelope encryption with your key. we'll include an architecture diagram in the security pack.
[00:58] Rajiv Singh: quick Q — are keys ever accessible by Redwood ops for troubleshooting?
[01:02] Samir Patel: short answer: no, not by default. with customer-managed KMS, Redwood cannot decrypt without key access. there is an exception path for emergency access but it's gated and auditable — it's in the SOC2 controls.
[01:15] Rajiv Singh: okay we'll want the exact process and a contact for emergency key escrow, if any.
[01:21] Maya Rios: noted, we'll send the emergency access runbook and the SOC2 control mapping.
[01:26] Jill Moreno: on SLAs, our operations team wants 99.95% uptime with 1 second p95 for the APIs. can Redwood commit to that on hosted?
[01:36] Samir Patel: that's aggressive for hosted at scale, especially with large context windows. Redwood generally offers SLA tiers — 99.9% for hosted API, and 99.95% for Dedicated reserved capacity. p95 of 1s depends on model and token sizes; for small prompts with our optimized runtime we can often hit sub-second p95 but not guaranteed for every workload.
[01:55] Jill Moreno: so the dedicated option would be the one to hit their SLA target?
[01:58] Samir Patel: yes, Dedicated with pinned models and reserved GPUs gives the most predictable latency and throughput. we can also set routing to a lower-cost fallback with different SLOs.
[02:06] Ellen Park: would that significantly change pricing?
[02:09] Maya Rios: Dedicated is a commitment contract — monthly or annual reserved capacity — so it generally increases base cost but lowers unit cost per token. we can provide an expected TCO comparison. I'll include a pricing worksheet that models your 6-month and 12-month commitments.
[02:22] Jill Moreno: budget committee prefers a firm price. is there an option for committed monthly usage rather than capacity?
[02:27] Maya Rios: yes, we have committed usage discounts (by tokens or compute hours) that sit between pure usage and reserved GPUs. we'll model both in the worksheet.
[02:35] Rajiv Singh: another security point: audit logs — how long can we retain request/response logs? and do you support redaction?
[02:42] Samir Patel: by default we retain logs 90 days in hosted; for enterprise we offer extended retention (customizable) and can enable PII redaction at ingestion. for private deployments you control retention entirely.
[02:53] Ellen Park: we need 2 years of tamper-evident audit logs for compliance. is that possible?
[02:58] Maya Rios: yes, on Dedicated/Private we can support 2 years; for hosted we can add an extended retention add-on — I'll detail costs.
[03:06] Jill Moreno: about the MSA — we had a clause around indemnity that our legal flagged. we proposed a cap tied to a single year of fees. standard practice?
[03:16] Ellen Park: yes we want liability capped to fees and carve-outs only for willful misconduct.
[03:22] Maya Rios: Redwood's standard MSA caps liability to fees for the prior 12 months; we can accept language around willful misconduct carve-outs. we'll send a redline showing that.
[03:30] Ellen Park: ok we'll review.
[03:33] Rajiv Singh: network diagrams — we need VPC peering details and egress patterns for our security review.
[03:39] Samir Patel: we'll attach architecture diagrams: VPC, private endpoints, and flow for KV cache and prefix caching. note — sometimes transcripts show 'KV cash' on our docs, ignore that, it's 'KV cache' — sorry, brain slip.
[03:50] (laughter)
[03:53] Jill Moreno: haha, noted. on data residency, can Redwood guarantee region locks for EU data?
[03:58] Maya Rios: yes, for Private deployments or Dedicated in regional zones we can pin data residency. Hosted has region options but not strict region locks unless part of an enterprise contract.
[04:10] Ellen Park: pricing approval path — who needs to sign? procurement or legal first?
[04:15] Jill Moreno: procurement will do initial PO and budget sign-off; legal wants the MSA/DPA finalized before PO is issued.
[04:21] Maya Rios: that aligns with Redwood's process — we'll prioritize the docs to avoid hold-ups.
[04:26] Rajiv Singh: technical bench — Samir, what do you need from us to run the latency/cost benchmarks?
[04:31] Samir Patel: a representative prompt set and sample payload sizes, expected concurrency, and a small test dataset for embedding/llm workloads. also credentials to hit a staging endpoint or a tarball we can simulate locally.
[04:43] Jill Moreno: I'll get that list from ops and share it via the secure link.
[04:47] Maya Rios: perfect, and we'll post the benchmark results to the shared folder with the spreadsheet. link will be included in the follow-up email.
[04:55] Ellen Park: on the DPA, one more ask: data deletion certification post-termination is required. can Redwood provide a certificate or attestation?
[05:03] Maya Rios: yes, we can provide a data disposition certificate for Private and Dedicated — for hosted we have a documented deletion process and audit logs; we can provide attestation upon request.
[05:14] Jill Moreno: if we do Dedicated, how fast can we spin up a pilot env for testing? two to three weeks?
[05:20] Samir Patel: with committed capacity, pilot can be provisioned within 10 business days typically, dependent on model onboarding and config. on-hosted we can give immediate test keys.
[05:30] Rajiv Singh: SLA credits — what's Redwood's approach?
[05:34] Maya Rios: credits are prorated service credits tied to downtime buckets; for enterprise deals we can negotiate specific remedies and runbooks.
[05:41] Ellen Park: and support response times?
[05:44] Samir Patel: standard support is next-business-day; enterprise support includes 1-hour P1 response and a named technical account manager.
[05:52] Jill Moreno: budget committee will want to see P&L impact; can you show committed vs on-demand cost over 12 months?
[05:58] Maya Rios: yes that will be in the pricing worksheet — we'll include committed vs on-demand scenarios plus break-even analysis.
[06:06] Jill Moreno: perfect. anything else?
[06:09] Ellen Park: last question — do you allow subprocessor disclosure and a list?
[06:12] Maya Rios: yes we maintain a subprocessors list and update cadence; we'll include the latest list and the subprocessor security memos.
[06:19] (pause)
[06:22] Maya Rios: okay, quick recap — Maya to send redlined MSA/DPA + security packet (SOC2/ISO/network diagram), Samir to run benchmark and share pricing worksheet, Peregrine to share prompt set and DPA mandatory edits, schedule follow-up week of 5/25.
[06:40] Jill Moreno: that matches our notes. thanks everyone.
[06:43] Rajiv Singh: thanks, talk soon.
[06:45] Ellen Park: thanks.
[06:47] Maya Rios: thanks all, we'll follow up with docs and links by Monday. bye.
[06:52] (call ends)
references: MSA/DPA redline: attachment in follow-up email
